finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the public POST /hooks/test handler passes a request-body URL straight to axios.post with no scheme, host, or IP validation. The attacker can make the server send POST requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints. The response status is returned, which gives a reachability oracle.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:20), attacker-controlled JSON body on the public router `pub`

trace.note: `pub` router is created without any auth middleware; only `admin` gets requireAdmin
req.body.callback is used directly as the axios.post URL
upstream status is returned to the caller, so internal hosts can be probed

finding.guards_checked: No auth on `pub` (requireAdmin is applied only via admin.use at line 12). No URL parsing, allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP block, or scheme check. axios follows redirects by default, so there is no redirect restriction either. The only file in the repo is routes.js, so I could not see how `pub` is mounted; an external auth middleware at mount time is possible but not visible. Not reported: GET /diagnostics/fetch (routes.js:15) also takes an unvalidated URL, but it sits behind requireAdmin at line 12, so I excluded it under the privilege rule.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback directly to axios.post, and routes.js:21 returns the upstream status. The `pub` router (routes.js:4) has no auth, because requireAdmin is applied only to `admin` (routes.js:12), and nothing validates the URL. The one caveat is that routes.js is the only file in the repo, so how `pub` is mounted can't be checked.
